opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexander Brown (employee ID E018) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E018.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alexander Brown (E018) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write access; admin requires that the employee's role owns the system, and Analyst does not own Payroll. Therefore the maximum is write, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record (E018): contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; admin is never allowed. Requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: Alexander Brown (E018) requests admin access to Payroll. Admin is never permitted: Analyst does not own Payroll, and contractors are never allowed admin. The two notes conflict on employment type (HR: full_time; Security: contractor with basic training). Applying the more restrictive applicable policy from the Security record (contractor with basic training maxes out at read), the maximum access is read. Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum, I grant the maximum of read.
